title: Polarity-selective domain wall propagation driven by spin-orbit torque
authors: Nobuyuki Umetsu, Michael Quinsat, Masaki Kado, Hiroki Tokuhira
abstract: Spatial variations in magnetic anisotropy impede the spin-orbit-torque-driven motion of chiral domain walls in perpendicularly magnetized nanowires. We show that the local geometry of a two-dimensional anisotropy landscape can select which wall polarity propagates under a given current. Micromagnetic simulations of spatially correlated random anisotropy landscapes generated by diffusion-based smoothing reveal different propagation outcomes for up--down and down--up walls within the same disorder realization. A single inclined anisotropy boundary isolates the mechanism: in the presence of the Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction, opposite wall polarities develop opposite current-induced tilts, producing different alignment with the boundary and hence different pinning strengths. Reversing the boundary inclination interchanges the pinned and propagating polarities. An extended collective-coordinate model captures this geometric selection and distinguishes the propagation threshold from the static pinning limit.
summary: This paper demonstrates that the local geometry of magnetic anisotropy can select the propagation direction of domain walls driven by spin-orbit torque. Using micromagnetic simulations and a 1D collective-coordinate model, the authors show that opposite wall polarities experience different pinning forces when encountering an inclined anisotropy boundary. This mechanism offers a pathway for controlling magnetic information storage via material design.
main_problem: The study investigates how spatial variations in magnetic anisotropy impede the spin-orbit-torque (SOT)-driven motion of chiral domain walls (DWs), demonstrating that the local geometry dictates which wall polarity propagates.
main_result: Opposite wall polarities exhibit qualitatively different pinning strengths near an inclined anisotropy boundary, leading to polarity-selective domain wall propagation. The critical current density ($j_c$) differs significantly between the two polarities.
method: The research employs micromagnetic simulations on random anisotropy landscapes and develops an extended one-dimensional collective-coordinate model (1DM) to capture the dynamics.
model_or_system: The system involves perpendicularly magnetized nanowires exhibiting PMA and DMI, modeled using the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation and simplified to a 1DM with coordinates $(\zeta, \phi, \chi)$. The anisotropy landscape is generated using diffusion-based smoothing of random noise.
key_observables: DW velocity, pinning strength, critical current density ($j_c$), and the DW tilt angle ($\chi$).
important_parameters: Anisotropy boundary angle ($\chi_0$), current density ($j$), and the anisotropy strength parameter ($\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes $ eta_{so}=0$ for main results, treats the DW width ($\lambda$) as constant, and uses the 1DM framework derived from the generalized Euler–Lagrange formalism.
figures_summary: Figures show DW snapshots and time evolution in random PMA landscapes, and the 1DM dynamics illustrate the difference in propagation thresholds ($j_c$) for up-down versus down-up walls as a function of the boundary angle $\chi_0$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing the general micromagnetic behavior in disordered systems to deriving a simplified 1DM model. It then uses this model to analytically determine the static pinning limit ($j_{	ext{stat}}$) and compares it to the dynamic propagation threshold ($j_c$), highlighting the geometric selection mechanism.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed, physics-based mechanism for controlling magnetic domain wall motion using engineered material disorder and spin-orbit torques, which is relevant to spintronics and magnetic memory applications.

Figure 4(b) shows the κ dependence of jc for both DW polarities, obtained from the 1DM for α = 0.03 and 0.5. As κ increases, jc increases for both polarities, and the splitting between the two thresholds becomes more pro- nounced. The lower jc at smaller α indicates that the propagation threshold depends on both the static pinning landscape and transient DW dynamics. A higher SOT- driven DW velocity at lower damping [19, 37] can allow the wall to cross the PMA boundary before reaching a pinned state.
